Which agent is waiting, and which branch still needs a push?

Vulcan Celox is an open-source terminal and local workspace for macOS. It brings Claude Code and Codex sessions, projects, commands, and notes into one app.

Vulcan CeloxOverview

Projects, tasks, terminals, and recent sessions, together at the same starting point.

From project to code changes.

When each agent lives in a different window and each project in another folder, context gets scattered. Celox brings your local work together and makes the connections visible.

Open your project

Find PHP sites, add Node projects, or open a folder. Each terminal starts in the right place.

Work with your agents

Choose Claude Code or Codex for that tab. Follow sessions, requests, files, and commands without switching tools.

Come back with context

Resume a session, read the terminal's memory, and see what changed before continuing.

A terminal for each session.

Open a shell or choose Claude Code or Codex for a tab. Name and color terminal tabs to identify open sessions, and link sticky notes to the work they belong to.

  • Named, color-coded tabs for each session
  • Sticky notes linked to terminal sessions and history
  • Split panes, output search, and a prompt library

PHP and Node in one workspace.

Use Lerd or Laravel Valet for local PHP development. Add Node projects, see their scripts, and open commands in the terminal. No PHP installed? Terminals, agents, and organization are still available.

Claude CodeCodexPHP + LaravelNode.jsGit
  • PHP sites, versions, and local HTTPS through your backend
  • Node projects and package.json scripts
  • Branches, worktrees, and agent history

Your workspace stays local.

The app reads local agent logs to organize context. It doesn't require an API key to follow Claude Code and Codex, and it doesn't write to their configuration folders.

Your data stays with you

Preferences, tasks, prompts, and memories are stored locally. Make a backup when you need one.

Connections with a purpose

PR and update checks have their own controls. AI documentation runs only when you request it, using your Anthropic key.

Transparency in the source

Read the project, licenses, and documentation. Celox is open source under the MIT license.

Use Celox in your language.

Choose Português (Brasil), English (US), or Español (España) in Settings. You don't need to install three separate apps.

Frequently asked questions

What is Vulcan Celox?

It is a free, open-source macOS app for terminals, Claude Code and Codex sessions, local projects, and notes. The stable release for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs is available on GitHub.

How do I identify a tab and return to a terminal from a sticky note?

Use Name and color in the tab bar to identify the session. Open a linked sticky note to see its terminal and return to the open tab or view the memory of a closed session.

Does Celox replace Claude Code or Codex?

No. It organizes projects, terminals, and sessions around the tools you already use. Your agents still run through their own programs and accounts.

Do I need an API key?

Not to read and follow local Claude Code and Codex sessions. The optional AI documentation feature uses your Anthropic key and runs only when you request it.

Can I edit files inside the app?

The Code screen is a read-only viewer with a tree, search, live following, and diffs. Use your external editor for changes. Celox doesn't promise file saving in that screen.

Do I need to install Lerd?

Only if you want to use it as the backend for local PHP sites. Laravel Valet is also supported. Node projects, terminals, agents, and organization work without either backend.

Which operating systems are supported?

The stable experience is built for macOS. Linux and Windows distributions are prereleases; check the requirements and limitations published in the repository.

What leaves my computer?

App data is local. Optional features contact external services, such as GitHub for PRs and versions and Anthropic for documentation you request. The agents themselves follow their own services and settings.

Is Codex tab pairing exact?

The link to a tab uses folder and timing. Sessions started almost together in the same folder can be matched to the wrong tab. This limitation is documented and doesn't change the per-tab decision to start an agent.

Is the project open source?

Yes. Celox source code is distributed under the MIT license. Third-party components keep their own licenses and notices in the repository.

Install Celox on your Mac.

Download the app, open a folder, and start with the tools you already know.

Download for macOS Read the installation guide

macOS 13 or later, Apple Silicon or Intel, and Python 3.9+. The app guides you through installing Python if needed. Claude Code, Codex, and environment backends are installed separately.

Version 1.4.0, universal for Apple Silicon and Intel, with all three languages. The app is not notarized by Apple.

  1. Download and extract the package

    Extract the universal ZIP and move Vulcan Celox.app to your Applications folder.

  2. Open Celox

    Choose your language and find your projects. Local data stays separate from the application.

  3. Open your first terminal

    Start with a shell or select Claude Code or Codex for that tab.
